Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turn. Attached is Acme's redline of the Order Form (v3) and a short memo from our legal team. Two core asks we need clarity on before we can sign: 

1) Training / retraining: the redline removes any broad training license. Acme needs confirmation that Redwood will not use Acme customer data to train models used outside of our account, and wants explicit language that any model improvements derived from Acme data remain inaccessible to other customers unless we opt in.

2) Feedback & telemetry: Acme is okay with aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement but wants a limited feedback license (time-bound and purpose-limited). They also want an operations handoff note: if models are updated using any of our data, we need a preview window and the option to reject changes for production traffic for 14 days.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a carve-out that: (a) prohibits cross-customer training for Acme data without express written opt-in, (b) provides a 14-day preview/fallback period for model updates affecting Acme, and (c) limits feedback use to service stability and non-commercial model improvement?

If you prefer, happy to set up a 30-min call with our procurement counsel next week.

Thanks,

Jordan / Sam —

Thanks for the summary. I reviewed Acme's redline and propose the following compromise language (high level):

1) Training prohibition: "Provider shall not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune models that are made available to other customers, partners, or the public, without Customer's prior written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Provider may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry for service reliability and performance monitoring, provided such data cannot be re-identified to Customer or its end users."

2) Preview / rollback: "If Provider intends to deploy model updates that may materially affect Customer's production outputs, Provider will provide Customer with a 14-calendar-day preview and an option to reject the update for Customer's production traffic. Provider will document the nature of the changes and provide test vectors. If Customer rejects, Provider will continue serving the prior model/variant for Customer's production traffic for 14 days while the parties remediate."

3) Feedback license: "Customer grants Provider a non-exclusive, time-limited (12 months), non-transferable license to use Customer Feedback (as defined) solely for improving Provider's inference service quality and reliability; Provider shall not use such Feedback to create models or datasets sold to third parties without Customer's express opt-in."

Operational notes / risks:
- Olga: the preview/blocking pattern is implementable but adds a manual gating step; it affects our SLA for releases and may increase maintenance overhead. We should limit preview requests to Major model upgrades (not routine patching).
- Karthik (legal ops): suggest we tie the 14-day rejection to explicit change-magnitude thresholds in the Order Form to avoid frequent gating.

Sam — if Acme is comfortable with the above, I can produce redline language to drop into the Order Form and propose a small playbook describing how the preview process will work (roles, test vectors, timing).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
